subject: Chemistry
question: Use the average bond enthalpies in the supplied table to estimate the enthalpy change for the combustion of methane: CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(g).

supplied_texts.title: Average bond enthalpies at 298 K (extract)
supplied_texts.text:
Bond / average bond enthalpy (kJ mol⁻¹)
C–H 414
O=O 498
C=O 804
O–H 463
supplied_texts.provenance: data table supplied with the question

response_text:
CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O

Bonds broken: four C–H bonds and two O=O bonds.
Energy absorbed = 4 × 414 + 2 × 498 = 2652 kJ mol⁻¹
Bonds formed: two C=O bonds and four O–H bonds.
Energy released = 2 × 804 + 4 × 463 = 3460 kJ mol⁻¹

ΔH = energy absorbed − energy released = 2652 − 3460 = +808 kJ mol⁻¹

The value is only an estimate, because average bond enthalpies are used.

faults.note: stem-eq (exact mode, all integers): 2652 − 3460 = −808; stated +808. The combustion is exothermic; the sign was dropped. [computed: C=-808 S=808 h=0 tau=0 -> does not hold; C=-808 S=808 h=0.5 tau=1/100 -> does not hold]
